content: Twenty years from now you will be more disappointed by the things that you didn't do than by the ones you did do.
author: Mark Twain
story:
There is a sharp, grounded clarity in this observation. Most human unhappiness exists in two places that don't currently exist: the past, which cannot be changed, and the future, which hasn't happened yet. Meanwhile, the only life you will ever experience is slipping past unnoticed.

Across his life and work, Mark Twain saw how easily we surrender our tranquility to fear, vanity, and distraction. Presence is not a rare mystical achievement; it is simply having the courtesy to show up for your own life. When you anchor your awareness in the immediate room and task, the frantic anxieties of the ego dissolve.
reflectionPrompt: What simple, everyday blessing in your immediate surroundings are you currently taking for granted?
